summary: joule-btp-extension exfiltrates host data and /etc/passwd to hardcoded ngrok endpoint at install time
details: setup.py defines a collect_and_exfiltrate() routine that fires during pip install (guarded by the PIP_BUILD_TRACKER / PIP_REQ_TRACKER environment variables pip sets on the build). It gathers the installer's hostname, current working directory, selected environment variables, and the contents of /private/etc/passwd and /private/etc/hosts, and enumerates files under the cwd and $VIRTUAL_ENV. The collected data is POSTed as JSON to a hardcoded ngrok-free.app URL and to http://127.0.0.1:4445/collect, and the raw /etc/passwd bytes are additionally POSTed to the same ngrok endpoint. setup.py also runs os.system("cat /private/etc/passwd") to echo the file into pip's install output. The destination is hardcoded and author-controlled; the installer never opts into or configures it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
